subject.name: Maths
subject.description: Grade 11 Semester 1 Mathematics develops algebraic reasoning, polynomial analysis, rational functions, counting methods, and probability. The course strengthens students' ability to model relationships, interpret functions and graphs, and solve realistic problems using mathematical structure and logic.

content.title: Unit 1 (Lo1)
content.description: This unit introduces polynomial functions and algebraic relationships, helping students understand the structure of expressions, the behavior of graphs, and the methods used to solve equations and analyze function properties.

concepts.title: Polynomial
concepts.description: This concept examines polynomial expressions and their structure, emphasizing terms, coefficients, degree, and the role of algebraic form in function behavior.

concepts.title: Absolute value
concepts.description: This concept explains how absolute value measures distance from zero and how it affects graphing, inequalities, and equation solving.

concepts.title: Inverse of a function
concepts.description: This concept explores how functions can be reversed and how inverse relationships help interpret equations, mappings, and graph symmetry.

concepts.title: Algebraic function
concepts.description: This concept introduces algebraic functions and shows how symbolic rules can represent patterns, relationships, and continuous mathematical behavior.

concepts.title: Operations with polynomials
concepts.description: This concept focuses on adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing polynomial expressions while connecting these operations to algebraic simplification and graph interpretation.

concepts.title: Roots of polynomial equations
concepts.description: This concept explains the meaning of roots and zeros, showing how solutions to polynomial equations relate to x-intercepts and the graph of a function.

concepts.title: Polynomial curve
concepts.description: This concept studies the shape of polynomial curves and how their turning points, end behavior, and intercepts communicate the underlying function.

concepts.title: Polynomial functions
concepts.description: This concept demonstrates how polynomial functions map inputs to outputs and how their equations and graphs reveal important mathematical patterns.

concepts.title: Degree of the function
concepts.description: This concept addresses how the degree of a polynomial determines its overall behavior, including the number of possible turning points and end behavior.

concepts.title: Attributes of a graph - turning points, symmetry, even/odd
concepts.description: This concept introduces key graph features such as turning points, symmetry, and even/odd behavior, which help interpret the structure of polynomial functions.

concepts.title: Polynomial in one variable
concepts.description: This concept focuses on polynomial expressions involving a single variable and how such expressions are analyzed, simplified, and solved.

concepts.title: Multiplicity
concepts.description: This concept examines repeated roots and their effect on the graph of a polynomial, including how multiplicity influences intercept behavior.

concepts.title: The Remainder Theorem
concepts.description: This concept explains how polynomial division can reveal remainders and how synthetic or long division helps evaluate functions without full expansion.

concepts.title: The Factor Theorem
concepts.description: This concept connects roots and factors, showing that if a value is a root, then the corresponding linear factor divides the polynomial exactly.

concepts.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.description: This concept demonstrates that continuous functions take every value between two outputs and why this idea is important for proving solutions and graph behavior.

concepts.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
concepts.description: This concept states that every nonzero polynomial has a complete set of roots in the complex number system and explains the significance of this result.

concepts.title: Descartes' Rule of Signs
concepts.description: This concept shows how the number of sign changes in a polynomial's coefficients helps predict the possible number of positive and negative real roots.

content.title: Unit 2 (Lo2)
content.description: This unit develops rational function analysis, focusing on how algebraic expressions behave near undefined values and how asymptotes describe the long-term shape of the graph.

concepts.title: Rational polynomial expressions
concepts.description: This concept introduces rational expressions and explains how numerator and denominator relationships create domains, restrictions, and simplified algebraic forms.

concepts.title: Sketch rational functions
concepts.description: This concept shows how to analyze intercepts, asymptotes, and end behavior to sketch the graph of rational functions accurately.

concepts.title: Vertical asymptotes of rational functions
concepts.description: This concept explains how factors in the denominator create vertical asymptotes and how these features represent discontinuities in the graph.

concepts.title: Horizontal asymptotes of rational functions
concepts.description: This concept examines how the relative degrees of the numerator and denominator determine a function's end behavior and horizontal asymptote.

concepts.title: An oblique asymptote or a slant asymptote
concepts.description: This concept introduces slant asymptotes, showing how a rational function can approach a non-horizontal line as x grows large in magnitude.

content.title: Unit 3 (Lo3)
content.description: This unit introduces counting techniques and combinatorics, helping students calculate possible outcomes, permutations, and combinations in practical and theoretical situations.

concepts.title: Fundamental Counting Principle
concepts.description: This concept introduces multiplication as a strategy for counting total outcomes when independent choices are made in sequence.

concepts.title: Permutations
concepts.description: This concept explains ordered arrangements and shows how the number of possible sequences is found when the order of items matters.

concepts.title: Combinations
concepts.description: This concept examines unordered selections and demonstrates how grouping objects without regard to order affects the counting process.

concepts.title: Factorials
concepts.description: This concept explains factorial notation and how it simplifies repeated multiplication in permutations, combinations, and probability counting.

content.title: Unit 4 (Lo4)
content.description: This unit explores binomial expansion and pattern-based reasoning, using Pascal's Triangle and the Binomial Theorem to model coefficients and combinations in algebra.

concepts.title: Pascal's Triangle
concepts.description: This concept illustrates a triangular number pattern that organizes coefficients and helps students recognize combinations and binomial expansion structure.

concepts.title: Binomial Theorem
concepts.description: This concept expands powers of binomials and connects algebraic expansion with coefficients, combinations, and pattern recognition.

content.title: Unit 5 (Lo5)
content.description: This unit introduces probability and chance-based thinking, including sample spaces, expected value, and compound events that model uncertainty and real-life decision-making.

concepts.title: Probability
concepts.description: This concept defines probability as the measure of likelihood and explains how outcomes are assigned numerical values in experiments and models.

concepts.title: Tree diagram
concepts.description: This concept uses branching diagrams to represent multi-step experiments and to organize possible outcomes clearly and systematically.

concepts.title: Compound events Probability
concepts.description: This concept combines multiple events to analyze dependent and independent outcomes, helping students calculate the probability of sequences and intersections.

concepts.title: Expected values
concepts.description: This concept explains how average outcomes are calculated in probabilistic situations and why expected value is useful in prediction and decision-making.

content.title: Revisions
content.description: This revision set consolidates the core ideas covered in the first part of the course, helping students revisit algebraic structure, graph interpretation, and foundational mathematical problem solving before the assessment.
